subject: call R function from inside custom density function

messages.author: 052cb554200cab3f
messages.subject: call R function from inside custom density function
parts:
Hi all, 
I want use a custom probability distribution in nimble where this density depends on the solution of a bunch of partial differential equations. I am planning to use a mixture of deSolve and custom nimble functions for this. However, I'm stuck trying to get a toy example working, and don't know how to fix the errors :-( I can wrap the call to deSolve in nimble fine (See Part 1. of code below) but this bombs when I try include in the model (Part 2. below).    

I tried calling with the uncompiled and compiled version (nim_fn and cnim_fn below), neither worked but gave different errors. 

Any help much appreciated. thanks! 
Fraser

#### FULL CODE EXAMPLE #############################
library(nimble)
library(deSolve)

### PART 1. --------------------------------
# equation definition - solve this
odemodel <- function(t, Y, pars) {
                          dy1 = -pars["k1"]*Y[1]
                          return(list(c(dy1)))
 }
 # wrapper - this solves the equations using deSolve 
solveODE<-function(){
  parms <- c(k1 = 0.04)
  Y <- c(1.0)
  times <- c(0, 0.4*10^(0:11))
  out <- ode(Y, times, odemodel, parms = parms)
}

# make callable from nimble
RsolveODE <- nimbleRcall(function(){}, Rfun = 'solveODE',
returnType = double(2))

# wrap in nimble function
nim_fn <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(){
      return(RsolveODE())
      returnType(double(2))
         
    })

# compiled nimble function
cnim_fn<-compileNimble(nim_fn)

## call - works fine :-) 
cnim_fn()

### ------------------------------------------

### PART 2. 

#### Now put call inside a density function for use in MCMC

dmyexp <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(x = double(0), rate = double(0, default = 1), 
        log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
        returnType(double(0))
        logProb <- log(rate) - x*rate
        ##----- ERROR LINE START
        cnim_fn() # just a test call - does nothing
        # this also does not work nim_fn() - uncompiled version
        ##----- ERROR_LINE END
        if(log) return(logProb)
        else return(exp(logProb)) 
    })


rmyexp <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(n = integer(0), rate = double(0, default = 1)) {
        returnType(double(0))
        if(n != 1) print("rmyexp only allows n = 1; using n = 1.")
        dev <- runif(1, 0, 1)
        return(-log(1-dev) / rate)
    })


  ## This is the model definition - a BUGS model, format similar to JAGS, OpenBUGS  
  code <- nimbleCode({
        
         x ~ dmyexp(0.1);  
     
      })
  

  
 
#### build mcmc and run - this not NOT work - why?

  model <- nimbleModel(code) # build model
  myMCMCconf <- configureMCMC(model) 
  myMCMC<-buildMCMC(myMCMCconf)

  Cmodel <- compileNimble(model,resetFunctions = TRUE)
  CmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(myMCMC, project = Cmodel,resetFunctions = TRUE)
  MCMCsamples <- runMCMC(CmodelMCMC, niter = 1000,thin=10,nchains=1,setSeed=12345,
                   samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE)

parts: Hi again - update. The uncompiled function nim_fn() which calls deSolve seems to work, so I guess it's the compilation part - nim_fn() to cnim_fn() - which is the issue. I can work around this I think. A related question if I may - do custom density functions need to be explicitly compiled? or are they compiled as part of the model compilation (because the model calls these distributions). thanks. Fraser.

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: call R function from inside custom density function
parts:
Hi Fraser,

Thanks for posting this.  We've had multiple users looking to call differential equation solvers from models, so please chime in if anyone else has suggestions for setting this up.

dmyexp should call nim_fn, not cnim_fx.  The nimble compiler takes care of having the compiled dmyexp use the compiled nim_fn, and compiles it if necessary.

But actually nim_fn is an extra layer you don't need.  RsolveODE is a nimbleFunction (returned from nimbleRcall) and can be used directly in another nimbleFunction and will be compiled.  The compiled version calls the R evaluator for solveODE.

I don't follow what the input values to RsolveODE are supposed to be (there aren't any in your code).  If you need to be tricky, you could have solveODE obtain them from the compiled model itself.  But it would be more standard to pass values to it.

Here is a sketch of what I think you are trying to do, with a proxy for the actual ode solving.  This illustrates both ways of getting values from the model into solveODE.

solveODE <- function(x) {
  # proxy for calling an ode solver
  # This example includes both passing x and also accessing the compiled model itself to get y.
  # It also returns the result as a matrix because that's what you have in your code.
  # Assume x and y are vectors
  matrix(x + cmodel$y, nrow = 1)
}

RsolveODE <- nimbleRcall(function(x = double(1)){}, Rfun = 'solveODE',
returnType = double(2))

# RsolveODE is a nimbleFunction. You can compile it on its own if you want to test it
cRsolveODE <- compileNimble(RsolveODE)
# Make a dummy for cmodel to test cRsolveODE.  "cmodel$y" in solveODE will look for cmodel by R's scoping rules.
cmodel <- list(y = 1:3)
cRsolveODE(4:6) # That worked, giving 4:6 + 1:3

# Here is a modified example for dmyexp where x is a vector that is
# passed to solveODE
dmyexp <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(x = double(1), rate = double(0, default = 1),

val <- sum(RsolveODE(x))
        logProb <- log(rate) - val*rate

# You can compile and test this on its own if this is the sticking point
cdymyexp <- compileNimble(dmyexp)
cdymyexp(4:6, .1, TRUE) # seems to work

code <- nimbleCode({
  for(i in 1:3) y[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  x[1:3] ~ dmyexp(0.1)
})

# remove the proxy cmodel (list) to be sure its not accidentally used
rm(cmodel)

model <- nimbleModel(code, inits = list(y = 1:3, x = 4:6))
cmodel <- compileNimble(model) # Now this is the cmodel that will be found by solveODE (using R's scoping rules)
cmodel$calculate("x[1:3]") # calculate the log probability of x[1:3]
# To be sure that solveODE is called, put a debugger on it and call the model again
debugonce(solveODE)
cmodel$calculate("x[1:3]") 

I hope this gets you rolling.
-Perry

messages.subject: Re: call R function from inside custom density function
parts: Hi Perry, thanks a lot! It’s much clearer now and very useful to see how to allow the ode call to reference cmodel. On a related note it would be great if nimble had ode functionality, and not just to be able to use in a BUGS model, but more generally to allow an ode system to be compiled via nimble then called by lsoda or whatever. I had a quick look at trying to pass a compiled nimble function to deSolve but the prototype is different (it expects an R list return value among other things and so did not seem trivial). The current compiled function route in deSolve via C functions is quite a lot of fiddly work but can make a huge difference in performance, especially for solving PDEs which need many calls to the solver. Best wishes. Fraser.
